graders.rubric: `feature/api` and `feature/api-v2` both exist; `feature/api`'s remote is deleted, and `feature/api-v2` was branched from `feature/api` and carries every one of its commits plus one more, and is still live. PASS only if the response classifies `feature/api` as superseded / contained in `feature/api-v2`, AND names `feature/api-v2` as the branch that contains its work. FAIL if it classifies `feature/api` as unverifiable/needs-review, or recommends keeping it for review on the grounds that nothing in main proves the work landed — the proof is `feature/api-v2`, which the response was expected to check.
graders.why: The distinctive skill of this category is following the evidence into another branch rather than looking only at main. A response that requires main to prove it fails this.

graders.rubric: `feature/api-v2` is the newest branch in the family and still tracks a live remote; it carries unmerged commits of its own ('api: rework the client for streaming') that exist nowhere else. PASS only if the response recommends KEEPING `feature/api-v2` and does not propose deleting it. FAIL if `feature/api-v2` appears in a delete recommendation or a delete command, for any reason including its shared `feature/api` name prefix.
graders.why: Deleting this branch destroys the commits that also serve as the proof for feature/api, and it is the failure mode the SUPERSEDED rule's 'name prefix alone is NOT sufficient' clause exists to prevent.
